findings.title: Containment escape through a case-sensitive NTFS directory: the ASCII-only fold is still a case-INSENSITIVE comparison
findings.repro: download to a NEW case-variant sibling 3/3 (file landed at cs\DLROOT\subN, outside root cs\dlroot, SHA matched the served file); download INTO an EXISTING unrelated sibling cs\Dlroot 1/1; upload READ of cs\UPROOT\secret-cs.txt from outside upload root cs\uproot 1/1 (the page received 'secret-cs.txt:26'). The per-directory case-sensitive flag was set WITHOUT elevation (fsutil setCaseSensitiveInfo); WSL-created directories have it by default. Pre-existing since develop (toLowerCase was also case-insensitive), not introduced by fix-1, but it is a real physical containment escape in this item's boundary.
findings.fix: Both sides are already realpath-canonicalized. realpath returns the on-disk casing for every existing component, so when the root exists, compare segments EXACTLY (case-sensitively) for the canonicalized prefix. Case-folding is only needed, if at all, when the root itself does not exist.

findings.title: GAP-296 not closed: download_file under concurrency still writes files into the user's platform ~/Downloads (outside every configured root), and into other calls' directories
findings.repro: same process, 2-4 tabs: 8 files in ~/Downloads across 18 concurrent trials (5/10 2-tab trials), 14 cross-dir writes; multi-process attach: 2/10 to ~/Downloads, 2/10 into another server's root. Root cause (live): the 'deny' reset does not survive detach (AFTERDENY 3/3), and outer-timeout-abandoned dispatches keep running inside the lock later, clicking with a stale downloadDir.
findings.fix: (1) Keep one long-lived browser-level CDP session per browser for download behavior (never detach it) and set behavior per call, or use Browser.setDownloadBehavior with an explicit browserContextId, and verify it persists. (2) Make the lock wait cancellable and part of the timeout budget, so a dispatch abandoned by the outer race never runs its click later. (3) A lock cannot cover multiple processes attached to one Chrome, so after completion also verify the reported path and treat any download event without a matching guid as a failure. (4) Add a unit test guarding the lock (mutant E1 survives) and fix the GAP-296 live test to require success and re-check ~/Downloads after a drain period.

findings.title: Concurrent download_file reliability: 0/47 same-process concurrent calls succeeded (2/3/4 tabs), each taking ~100s. This is far worse than the disclosed "more often hits the retry loop"; concurrent downloads are effectively broken.
Test integrity: no unit test guards the GAP-296 lock (E1 mutant survives); the posix no-reject path is untested on win32 (P11 survives); fix-1's GAP-296 live check passes on total failure.
